title: Hopwood Triangle road restrictions scrapped after unanimous Heywood Township vote
body:
Councillors have voted unanimously to end the Hopwood Triangle traffic trial affecting Middleton Road and Magdala Street in Heywood, following months of opposition from residents.

The decision was taken at an extraordinary Heywood Township meeting on Monday night. The temporary measures introduced as part of the trial will now be removed, while the restriction preventing heavy goods vehicles from parking on Coronation Avenue will remain in place.

The trial had become one of the most contentious local highways issues in Heywood. According to figures presented by Reform UK, around 700 people responded to the original consultation and 86 per cent opposed the scheme. Despite that result, the trial was approved and introduced.

Residents subsequently raised concerns about congestion, access, road safety and the impact on nearby businesses. People living on Manchester Road also argued that they had not been included in the original consultation despite experiencing traffic displaced from the affected streets.

The timing of the trial was another source of criticism. The measures were introduced during the quieter summer holiday period, with opponents warning that the full effect would become clearer once schools reopened and normal traffic levels returned.

More than 50 residents attended the extraordinary meeting, according to an account supplied to Rochdale Daily by Reform UK. The size of the room at the former police station became an issue as people tried to gain access to a public meeting concerning their own streets.

Reform UK said tensions rose and the meeting came close to being suspended before councillor Stuart Crawford intervened and urged the meeting to move on to a decision. Residents had already heard the highways presentations, and Crawford argued that councillors should proceed to the vote rather than risk the meeting ending without an outcome.

The vote was then taken, with every councillor present supporting an end to the trial.

The decision means the temporary restrictions on Middleton Road and Magdala Street are due to be removed. The separate restriction on heavy wagons parking on Coronation Avenue will remain.

The cost of the trial is also likely to remain a point of debate. Reform UK said a figure of £110,000 was presented for installing the temporary measures. Rochdale Daily has asked for confirmation of the final cost of the scheme, including whether removing the measures will create any additional expense.

Reform UK also said the original scheme had been approved in November by Labour councillors Angela Brown, Paul O'Neil, Peter Hodgkinson, Peter Joinson, Susan Emmott and Liam O'Rourke, despite the consultation opposition. Labour representatives and Rochdale Council are entitled to respond to that account.

Whatever the political arguments surrounding the scheme, the final decision represents a significant victory for residents who continued to object after the trial began. Their concerns remained on the agenda until an extraordinary meeting was called and councillors ultimately voted to end the measures.

Reform UK described the result as 'people power in action' and thanked residents who attended the meeting, responded to the original consultation and continued to raise concerns.

Rochdale Daily has previously reported that the Hopwood Triangle trial included changes around Middleton Road and Manchester Road, as well as restrictions affecting surrounding residential streets. At that stage the measures were expected to remain in place until Heywood Township formally voted on their future. That vote has now taken place, and the trial has been brought to an end.
excerpt: Heywood Township councillors have voted unanimously to end the Hopwood Triangle traffic trial after sustained opposition from residents, while the Coronation Avenue HGV parking restriction will remain.
source_name: Reform UK statement supplied to Rochdale Daily
